newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-GRIFFIN OUT TO PROVE JONES ISN'T THE BEST.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-GRIFFIN OUT TO PROVE JONES ISN'T THE BEST.

text.p: Roy Jones Jr claims to be the best "pound for pound" fighter in the world but Montell Griffin intends to prove him wrong Friday.

"I respect him, you can't but respect him," Griffin said earlier this week in the run-up to his fight against the undefeated Jones, who will be defending his World Boxing Council (WBC) light heavyweight crown.
"But he has got people brainwashed, believing something that he ain't," said Griffin. "I say he is a good fighter, but not fantastic.
"He hasn't been put to the test, he hasn't fought anybody. He is going to fight somebody Friday. Then we will see how good he is."

Griffin, who is 26-0 with 18 wins inside the distance, is not the only one who sees vulnerability in the flashy and charismatic Jones, 34-0 with 29 inside the distance. The challenger's trainer, Hall of Famer Eddie Futch, sees it, too.

"I have seen great fighters down through the years and no matter how great, there is somebody out there who can beat them," said the 85-year-old Futch, who trained both Joe Frazier and Ken Norton to victory over Muhammad Ali.
"I always look for the weakness. Nobody is perfect and that is what we are going after," said Futch, who has trained 20 world champions.
"Roy Jones can do it all if he has the right opponent in front of him," Futch said. "He does very well against fighters who walk to him, as opposed to the boxer type."
Futch has trained the 26-year-old Griffin since his first pro fight in 1993 and says he is the type of fighter who can find the 28-year-old Jones's weaknesses and exploit them.

"Against Montell Griffin he will have an unorthodox boxer in front of him," said Futch. "Montell can box both right and left-handed. He is not a fighter who depends on one punch. He throws multi-punches in combinations.
"I think Montell is a very much underrated fighter," Futch said.
"He hasn't had the exposure because his style is not sensational, but his results are what people fail to look at.
"He doesn't have the flashy style of a Roy Jones, but he does have a style that is very difficult which Jones will find out when the bell rings," Futch said.
Jones won the then-vacant WBC crown by outpointing Mike McCallum last November.
Also on the card, David Reid, America's lone Olympic champion from last year's Atlanta Games, will make his pro debut against Sam Calderon, 10-0.
